title: 5.9 A 21-to-31 GHz DPD-Less Quadrature RFDAC with Invariant Impedance and Scalable LO Leakage
problem: RF digital-to-analog converters (RFDACs) for mm-wave wireless transmitters (high-order QAM, wideband modulation) suffer nonlinearity increasing with frequency due to: (1) varied output impedance across unit array vs. baseband code, (2) distributed parasitics, (3) LO leakage. Existing solutions—DPD (complex, frequency-dependent), open-loop linearization (PVT-variant), self-calibration (loop-response-limited)—are inadequate; extra bits added for intrinsic nonlinearity compensation waste power in high-GS/s baseband.
motivation: mm-Wave wireless systems (5G/6G) demand broadband high-linearity RF signal generation; traditional DPD complexity and cost limit deployment; intrinsic linearization is critical for power efficiency.
method: This millimeter-wave converter operates from 21 to 31 GHz and maintains linear signal output without software correction by using two design techniques. First, it keeps the output impedance constant regardless of the input signal, preventing impedance variations from distorting the signal. Second, it automatically suppresses the local oscillator signal (the reference frequency) from leaking into the output, adapting to temperature and voltage variations without requiring feedback loops.
key_novelty: A millimeter-wave converter that delivers natural linearity from 21 to 31 GHz through constant output impedance and adaptive local oscillator leakage suppression, eliminating the need for digital signal correction.
contributions: High-linearity support for high-order QAM without complex baseband circuits
limitations: Abstract does not provide SNDR, ACPR, EVM metrics, power consumption, die area, or comparison with state-of-art DPD-based and other linearization approaches at similar frequencies.
primary_theme: intrinsically linear DPD-less mm-wave RFDAC with invariant impedance
